claims.text: Post-solidification heat treatment of Cu-doped equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi induces a uniform, stable dispersion of nanoscale copper precipitates.
Nanoscale copper precipitates serve as highly conductive heat-transfer channels in the HEA.
The copper precipitates pin grain boundaries and thereby preserve mechanical integrity.
The Cu-doped equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi alloy has a homogeneous microstructure before post-solidification processing.
The proposed treatment is approximately 600°C for 1–2 hours under an inert atmosphere.
Optimized thermal ramping and holding protocols can control copper-precipitate nucleation and avoid coarsening.
The intervention will remain effective at service temperatures of 600–800°C under cyclic mechanical loading typical of plasma-facing components.
The treatment produces uniformly distributed nanoscale copper precipitates in the HEA matrix.
Copper has sufficiently high intrinsic thermal conductivity for copper nanoprecipitates to improve heat transport through the alloy.
A dispersed population of copper nanoprecipitates creates continuous heat-transfer channels.
A coherent nanoprecipitate distribution can help retain a fine microstructure and mechanical integrity under thermal and mechanical stress.
The treated alloy will have greater bulk effective thermal conductivity than untreated homogeneous HEA intermediate layers.
The treated alloy will maintain tensile strength at elevated temperature.
The treated alloy will resist cyclic load-induced degradation.
Conventionally processed Cu-doped AlCoCrFeNi HEAs have lower effective thermal conductivity than the proposed heat-treated material.
Conventionally processed Cu-doped AlCoCrFeNi HEAs are susceptible to microstructural coarsening under reactor operating conditions.
Performance outside 600–800°C or during extended high-temperature dwell may differ from the predicted performance.
Precipitate coarsening may limit the long-term conductivity and structural benefits during prolonged cyclic loading.
